claims.text: The starting material is an AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Internal colony boundaries in the starting alloy are susceptible to microcracking during room-temperature tensile loading.
The proposed intervention is annealing at approximately 600°C for 10–15 minutes under inert atmosphere, followed by rapid quenching.
Approximately 600°C is near a secondary-phase precipitation range suitable for forming B2 nanoprecipitates in this alloy.
The annealing treatment will produce coherent B2 nanoprecipitates.
The B2 nanoprecipitates will form exclusively along internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Short annealing duration and rapid quenching will prevent precipitate overgrowth and non-selective precipitation.
Boundary-localized B2 nanoprecipitates will enhance local interfacial cohesion.
Boundary-localized B2 nanoprecipitates will act as crack arrestors.
The B2 nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The proposed boundary reinforcement will delay crack nucleation and propagation.
The treatment will increase yield strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony alloy.
The treatment will increase ultimate tensile strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony alloy.
The treatment will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony alloy.
The unmodified alloy typically undergoes early internal-boundary microcrack initiation and propagation leading to brittle room-temperature tensile failure.
Precipitate growth within grains or loss of precipitate coherency could undermine the proposed strength and ductility improvements.
